cases.title: Night Ferry cut-out ticket
cases.audience: Passengers on a fictional evening river ferry
cases.use_context: Small perforated-style admission card held at the gangway and kept as a souvenir; read at 20-40 cm
cases.user_goal: Confirm departure, boarding side, cabin and demo booking reference before joining the queue
cases.content_basis: FICTIONAL_DEMO：Invented Night Ferry service, fictional sailing time, pier, cabin, booking reference and terms; no real transport operator or ticket is represented.
cases.visual_intent: The ticket's central porthole and wave edge are actual EVEN_ODD cut-outs revealing a contrasting backing; the silhouette carries the ferry identity while a strict information grid remains uncut.

documented_evidence.supports: Path commands, viewBox, fit and direction-independent EVEN_ODD holes

cases.boundary_probe: Before composing final copy, verify that two same-direction closed contours create the intended hole, the backing is visible through it and no anti-aliased fringe cuts into the adjacent text. Keep this probe in temp evidence.
cases.independence_rationale: A true multi-contour vector mask is the visual and functional core of the ticket; no other case uses path cut-outs as its primary technique.

criteria.condition: Departure time, fictional pier, boarding side, cabin and booking reference are complete and legible.
criteria.method: Text inventory and hand-held-scale review.

criteria.condition: The porthole and wave cut-outs reveal the intended backing and have clean, intentional edges.
criteria.method: Inspect cut-out boundaries at 200% and compare against a flat reference mask.

criteria.condition: No text intersects a cut-out or is clipped by the ticket silhouette.
criteria.method: Inspect every text-to-path boundary and canvas edge.

criteria.condition: The service and code are clearly identified as fictional demo content.
criteria.method: Read footer and booking label.

cases.title: Crosswind cycling route poster
cases.audience: Occasional urban cyclists planning a fictional low-traffic route
cases.use_context: Portrait poster at a fictional bike cooperative and community noticeboard; viewed first at 2 metres then approached for turns
cases.user_goal: Follow the demo route in order, recognise key turn types and find the start, finish and caution point
cases.content_basis: FICTIONAL_DEMO：Invented Crosswind route through invented streets, five fictional turns, demo distance and caution note; not a navigable map or safety-certified route.
cases.visual_intent: Route arrows are separate transformed DSL modules rotated and translated around explicit origins, forming a diagonal path through a strict typographic grid; the geometry reads as motion without becoming an unreadable map.

technique.name: ordered affine translate/rotate/scale with explicit origins

documented_evidence.supports: Transform syntax, multiplication order, units, origins and alignment

cases.boundary_probe: Verify the documented order with a small asymmetric module: translate then rotate about a non-central origin must land at the calculated point. Confirm that transforms do not reserve extra layout space and check parent clipping.
cases.independence_rationale: This case is built from transformed modules and order-sensitive coordinate mapping, unlike clipping, filters or proportional layout.

criteria.condition: Start, finish, five ordered turn labels, demo distance and caution note are complete and readable.
criteria.method: Route inventory and full-size review.

criteria.condition: Arrow angles and endpoints visually continue the intended route order without intersecting labels.
criteria.method: Inspect transformed geometry against calculated endpoint coordinates.

criteria.condition: No arrow or rotated label is accidentally clipped by its layout parent or the canvas.
criteria.method: Inspect each transform's visible bounds at 100%.

criteria.condition: A prominent demo/not-for-navigation notice prevents real-world routing reliance.
criteria.method: Read header and footer notices.

cases.title: Glasshouse visitor information panel
cases.audience: Visitors entering a fictional botanical glasshouse, including people who need calm, clear orientation
cases.use_context: Landscape information panel mounted beside the entrance; read at 0.5-1.5 metres with a planted background represented in DSL
cases.user_goal: Understand opening route, three demo climate zones, photography rule and where to ask for help
cases.content_basis: FICTIONAL_DEMO：Invented Lumen Glasshouse with three fictional climate rooms, demo route and visitor rules; no real facility or botanical guidance is asserted.
cases.visual_intent: A translucent information card sits over a DSL-built layered foliage background; BackdropFilter softens only the already-painted background while the route and typography remain sharp.

technique.name: BackdropFilter Gaussian blur over existing background

documented_evidence.supports: Backdrop blur versus subtree blur and existing-background requirement

cases.boundary_probe: Render a controlled probe with colour blocks behind and in front of the filter. Only the prior background should blur, the clipped panel edge should stay bounded and foreground glyphs should remain sharp.
cases.independence_rationale: The subject of the filter is already-painted backdrop content, producing a glass information surface; this is distinct from blurring a self-contained foreground subtree.

criteria.condition: Route, three climate-zone names, photography rule and help point are complete and sharp.
criteria.method: Text inventory and 100% foreground inspection.

criteria.condition: Blur is visible only in the intended glass panel and does not soften route lines, labels or the outer border.
criteria.method: Compare background, panel-edge and foreground regions at 200%.

criteria.condition: Panel contrast remains sufficient in the brightest intended background area without adding an opaque fill that defeats the technique.
criteria.method: Inspect each panel region and local background luminance in a review copy.

criteria.condition: Fictional facility and demo-information labels are readable.
criteria.method: Inspect header and footer.

cases.title: Low Tide Observatory depth poster
cases.audience: Families and students attending a fictional coastal-observatory open evening
cases.use_context: Portrait poster at a fictional visitor centre; viewed at 1-4 metres and approached for the demonstration schedule
cases.user_goal: Understand the shallow-to-deep visual theme, identify the three demo activities and find start time and meeting point
cases.content_basis: FICTIONAL_DEMO：Invented Low Tide Observatory event, fictional activity names, times and meeting point; abstract depth bands are illustrative, not measured ocean data.
cases.visual_intent: Three DSL-built wave layers move from crisp foreground to deliberately blurred distant layers using ImageFiltered; sharp type and activity cards sit above the depth field to preserve utility.

technique.name: ImageFiltered subtree Gaussian blur with automatic output bounds

documented_evidence.supports: ImageFiltered syntax and automatic sigma-based bounds
Gaussian subtree blur and automatic output bounds

cases.boundary_probe: Probe nested filtered wave bands with increasing sigma. Verify each subtree blurs independently, CLAMP avoids hard transparent repeats and sigma-based margins are not clipped by an outer Stack.
cases.independence_rationale: The case filters complete foreground subtrees to construct spatial depth; it does not sample a backdrop, and its blur levels encode the visual concept rather than merely adding an effect.

criteria.condition: Three demo activities, start time, meeting point and fictional event label are complete and sharp.
criteria.method: Copy inventory and full-size review.

criteria.condition: Foreground, middle and distant wave layers show three visibly different blur levels in the intended order.
criteria.method: Inspect matched wave samples at 200% and compare edge softness.

criteria.condition: Blur output margins are intact and no band creates a hard transparent cut-off or canvas-edge artifact.
criteria.method: Inspect every filtered layer boundary and outer canvas edge.

criteria.condition: Abstract depth graphics are labelled illustrative rather than measured data.
criteria.method: Read diagram caption.

cases.title: Two Lantern Theatre cast billboard
cases.audience: Potential audience members choosing a fictional community-theatre production
cases.use_context: Landscape billboard at a fictional arts venue; viewed from across a piazza before approaching for cast and dates
cases.user_goal: Identify the play, sense its two-sided conflict, see performance dates and find the fictional venue
cases.content_basis: FICTIONAL_DEMO：Invented Two Lantern Theatre production 'The Other Side of Noon', invented cast names, fictional dates and venue; all portrait geometry is original DSL construction.
cases.visual_intent: Two monochrome DSL portrait silhouettes overlap in the centre; ColorFiltered blend modes create controlled cobalt/coral duotone regions while the title and dates remain outside the blend zone.

technique.name: ColorFiltered with controlled Skia blend modes

documented_evidence.supports: Color filters versus blur, opacity and backdrop filtering

cases.boundary_probe: Probe two flat DSL colours under the intended blend mode, then apply it to overlapping silhouette subtrees. Confirm the blend changes only the intended subtree, transparent gaps do not acquire surprising fill and the title remains unfiltered.
cases.independence_rationale: Blend-mode colour transformation, not Gaussian blur or transparency alone, produces the central visual; the technique is tied to the production's two-sided conflict.

criteria.condition: Play title, fictional venue, dates and complete invented cast list are present and readable.
criteria.method: Copy inventory and full-size/detail review.

criteria.condition: The two portraits read as a deliberate cobalt/coral conflict with a visible blended overlap.
criteria.method: Inspect flat portrait regions and central overlap at 200%.

criteria.condition: Title, cast and date rail are unfiltered, unclipped and maintain clean edges.
criteria.method: Inspect boundaries between the blend zone and typography.

criteria.condition: Production, venue and cast are clearly labelled fictional demo content.
criteria.method: Read footer and header demo notice.

cases.title: Fix-It Club inline workshop leaflet
cases.audience: Adults attending a fictional community repair workshop for the first time
cases.use_context: A5 portrait leaflet handed out at sign-in and read seated at a workbench
cases.user_goal: Bring the right items, follow safety steps in order and understand what help is available at each demo station
cases.content_basis: FICTIONAL_DEMO：Invented Fix-It Club with three fictional repair stations, demo tools list and beginner safety steps; no real safety certification or repair instruction is claimed.
cases.visual_intent: Short instructions are genuine mixed text flows: DSL-built icons inside WidgetSpan stay inline with wrapped sentences, while station rows and a tools checklist provide separate reading structures.

documented_evidence.supports: Text nesting, paragraph scope, Raw and WidgetSpan rules
Inheritance, inline alignment and shared paragraph flow

cases.boundary_probe: Use an asymmetric 22 px icon inside a two-line mixed English/Chinese sentence. Verify it follows line wrapping, aligns to MIDDLE rather than the line box bottom, preserves intended spaces and does not split or clip at line boundaries.
cases.independence_rationale: Inline widgets participate in paragraph layout and wrapping, which is a different technical mechanism from placing icons in Rows, Stacks or transformed containers.

criteria.condition: Demo welcome, three station descriptions, tools checklist and four ordered safety steps are complete and readable.
criteria.method: Copy inventory and A5-scale review.

criteria.condition: Inline icons stay within the sentence flow, remain aligned to text and do not become detached at wraps.
criteria.method: Inspect every multi-line instruction at 200%.

criteria.condition: Raw spacing between mixed-script fragments is preserved without accidental formatting newlines or trim.
criteria.method: Compare intended strings with rendered line breaks and spacing.

criteria.condition: The leaflet labels its guidance as fictional demo content and avoids certified-safety claims.
criteria.method: Read safety heading and footer.

cases.title: Hand & Vessel fair pattern wrap
cases.audience: Visitors and makers at a fictional ceramics fair
cases.use_context: Wide entrance banner above a fictional craft-market counter; read at 2-6 metres with the pattern functioning as recognition rather than fine detail
cases.user_goal: Recognise the fair, find demo opening hours and locate the fictional maker hall
cases.content_basis: FICTIONAL_DEMO：Invented Hand & Vessel fair, fictional date, hours and hall location. A small original abstract vessel/arc tile is planned as a supporting asset; the banner structure, motifs, typography and information remain DSL-led.
cases.visual_intent: A repeating original tile creates a continuous ceramic-pattern field, explicitly fitted and scaled; large DSL title panels and a location block interrupt the field so it never competes with essential information.

technique.name: Image repeat with explicit fit and pixel-density scale

documented_evidence.supports: Image source, repeat, fit, scale and tile limits
Logical size, scale and repeat-count limits

supporting_assets.role: 仅作为Image repeat局部纹样；横幅主体结构、文案与信息区均为DSL

cases.boundary_probe: Confirm the small Data URI decodes, default SCALE_DOWN versus explicit FILL behaviour is understood, scale changes logical tile spacing as calculated, repeat stays below resource limits and no visible seam or unintended upscaling artifact appears.
cases.independence_rationale: A raster tile is procedurally repeated and scaled to generate the field; all other cases use layout, vector geometry, text flow, filters or compositing as their core method.

criteria.condition: Fair name, fictional date, hours and maker-hall location are complete and readable.
criteria.method: Copy inventory and distance-scale review.

criteria.condition: The pattern repeats at the planned density with consistent spacing and no unintended gap, seam or clipped tile at banner edges.
criteria.method: Inspect tile joins across the field at 200%.

criteria.condition: Title and location panels fully interrupt the pattern so essential text sits on clean fields.
criteria.method: Inspect every panel boundary and text background.

criteria.condition: DSL remains the primary construction; the supporting tile is recorded as original and fictional/demo, not external artwork.
criteria.method: Inspect final DSL structure and asset record after authorized execution.

cases.title: Blue Hour sky-orientation dial
cases.audience: First-time visitors at a fictional community observatory open night
cases.use_context: Square printed orientation card handed out at a fictional telescope queue; read outdoors at dusk with a small torch
cases.user_goal: Read the demo event timeline, find the three activity zones and understand the dial's direction labels
cases.content_basis: FICTIONAL_DEMO：Invented Blue Hour open night with fictional 18:30-21:00 schedule and zones. The dial is an orientation graphic, not a real star chart, weather forecast or astronomical prediction.
cases.visual_intent: A radial twilight field and a sweep-gradient outer dial surround a clear central schedule; aligned stops and angular bounds create the visual transition while labels and zone keys stay outside the gradient.

technique.name: radial and sweep gradients with explicit stops and angles

documented_evidence.supports: Gradient types, parameters, stop rules and type-specific constraints

cases.boundary_probe: Verify radial center/radius and sweep start/end angles in a probe with labelled sectors. Check stops count matches colours, all stops are nondecreasing and direction labels align with the actual rendered angular boundaries.
cases.independence_rationale: Continuous gradient fields with radial/angular parameterisation generate the composition; no bitmap repeat, filter or path mask is used as the primary visual mechanism.

criteria.condition: Fictional event hours, three activity zones, meeting point and demo notice are complete and readable.
criteria.method: Copy inventory and torch-lit low-brightness review of a copy.

criteria.condition: Radial and sweep fields meet cleanly with no banding artifact severe enough to obscure structure, and all stops/angles render as intended.
criteria.method: Inspect matched angular and radial samples at 200%.

criteria.condition: Direction and zone labels remain outside gradient colour transitions and do not rely on colour alone.
criteria.method: Grayscale review and label-to-sector comparison.

criteria.condition: The dial is explicitly labelled a fictional orientation graphic, not a real star chart.
criteria.method: Read centre caption and footer.

cases.title: Repair Commons modular timetable board
cases.audience: Residents checking a fictional neighbourhood repair-café programme
cases.use_context: A3 landscape board at a fictional community hall; three equal programme columns must remain readable when printed or reduced for a noticeboard photo
cases.user_goal: Choose a demo workshop by day and time, find the room and understand whether advance sign-up is needed
cases.content_basis: FICTIONAL_DEMO：Invented Repair Commons with six demo sessions, fictional rooms, times and sign-up rules; no real community service is represented.
cases.visual_intent: Proportional day bands and aspect-ratio-locked icons sit above three finite Flexible columns; the layout derives order from constraints rather than hundreds of absolute positions and remains balanced at different reductions.
cases.medium: A3 landscape modular community timetable board

technique.name: constraint-aware AspectRatio, FractionallySizedBox and Flex allocation

documented_evidence.supports: Flex allocation, proportional boxes and finite constraint requirements
Parent constraints, overflow and proportional layout distinctions

cases.boundary_probe: Build the module at full size and one reduced-width probe using the same nested constraints. Verify three columns stay equal, aspect-ratio icons do not distort, long titles wrap inside their allocation and no Expanded/Flexible receives an unbounded main axis.
cases.independence_rationale: The work's integrity comes from reusable constraint relationships and finite flex/proportional sizing, not decorative variation; the reduced-width probe directly tests that mechanism.

criteria.condition: Six demo sessions show matching day, time, title, room and sign-up rule with no swapped values.
criteria.method: Session-table reconciliation and full-size review.

criteria.condition: Three day columns remain aligned and balanced, with all six sessions in the correct column.
criteria.method: Inspect shared column edges and row order.

criteria.condition: A reduced-width test shows stable proportions, undistorted icons and wrapped text without overlap or clipping.
criteria.method: Generate a temp-only reduced constraint probe after authorization and compare geometry.

criteria.condition: The board clearly identifies the programme and sign-up rules as fictional demo information.
criteria.method: Inspect header and footer.

cases.title: Shadow Lab eclipse-night poster
cases.audience: Curious teenagers and adults considering a fictional community astronomy evening
cases.use_context: Portrait poster at a fictional library and school noticeboard; viewed at 1-4 metres and approached for the demonstration programme
cases.user_goal: Recognise the eclipse theme, understand that activities are demonstrations, and find fictional start time and meeting place
cases.content_basis: FICTIONAL_DEMO：Invented Shadow Lab evening with fictional light-and-shadow demonstrations, time and location. The orbital graphic is conceptual and does not depict a predicted eclipse or real celestial positions.
cases.visual_intent: Translucent orbital discs overlap in a Stack; Opacity groups and ClipOval masks create a luminous eclipse-like focal form while a sharp programme column keeps the poster useful.

technique.name: Stack, Opacity and ClipOval layer compositing

documented_evidence.supports: Stack clipping, Opacity range and oval clipping

cases.boundary_probe: Use two overlapping translucent circles and one opacity group. Verify layer order, group opacity versus per-layer opacity and anti-aliased oval boundaries; ensure no ancestor Stack clips intended orbital overhang.
cases.independence_rationale: The focal form depends on draw order, grouped alpha and oval masks; it uses neither gradient shaders, blend colour filters nor Gaussian blur, and its transparency must be checked mathematically as well as visually.

criteria.condition: Event name, fictional start time, meeting place and three demo activities are complete and readable.
criteria.method: Copy inventory and full-size review.

criteria.condition: Orbital overlaps show the intended cumulative transparency and clear layer order without muddying the focal rim.
criteria.method: Compare overlap regions to planned alpha/colour calculations at 200%.

criteria.condition: ClipOval edges are smooth and no intended orbital extension is clipped accidentally.
criteria.method: Inspect all oval and Stack boundaries.

criteria.condition: The poster labels the celestial graphic as conceptual demo artwork, not a predicted eclipse.
criteria.method: Read graphic caption and footer.
